item.title: Chemical leak in Toledo forces evacuations, shelter-in-place
item.description: A massive chemical leak in Toledo, Ohio, is forcing some people out of their homes while others have been told to shelter in place.

item.title: Witkoff blasted for calling Putin a "humanitarian"
item.description: After special envoy Steve Witkoff told Putin he was a "humanitarian" for releasing a U.S. citizen deemed to have been wrongfully detained, GOP Sen. John Cornyn responded, "No. Putin is a stone cold killer."

item.title: American Stephen Hubbard released by Russia, Trump confirms
item.description: Steve Witkoff lauded Vladimir Putin as "a humanitarian" as Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, an American deemed wrongfully detained by the U.S., after more than 4 years in prison.

item.title: DOJ watchdog declines investigation in Reflecting Pool case
item.description: Hearn's lawyers complain the inspector general has referred the case to the Office of Professional Responsibility, a unit that was largely gutted and lacks independence.

item.title: Voters sound off before Kansas Senate debate between Roger Marshall and Adam Hamilton
item.description: The Kansas Senate race is becoming increasingly competitive between incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall and Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton. They will go head-to-head on the debate stage Wednesday. CBS News reporter Katrina Kaufman spoke with voters about the race.

item.title: DOJ asks Supreme Court to allow border wall construction in Big Bend region
item.description: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to lift a lower court injunction that temporarily blocked the Trump administration from building a border wall and related infrastructure in the Big Bend Sector.

item.title: AI is advancing rapidly. Who's keeping it in check?
item.description: As AI advances at a rapid pace, tech leaders are weighing how to manage its risks while staying ahead in the race against China. Jo Ling Kent speaks with some of the biggest names in tech about their plans for keeping AI in check and addressing its potential dangers.

item.title: Pope Leo won't need more treatment after cancer surgery, doctors say
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will not need any further treatment after having lung cancer surgery, his doctors said in a statement.

item.title: No further treatment needed for Pope Leo after cancer surgery, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo won't need further treatment after his surgery for lung cancer, the Vatican announced on Wednesday. CBS News foreign correspondent Chris Livesay reports.

item.title: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
item.description: Iran says the U.S. is seeking changes to a seven-day ceasefire proposal Trump rejected last month as indirect talks continue.

item.title: Top DOJ official asks judges to step aside from immigration cases
item.description: A top official at the Justice Department is attempting to disqualify two Minnesota federal judges from a pair of cases related to immigration.

item.title: New Mexico AG accuses Epstein's lawyer, accountant of concealing crimes
item.description: New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed a lawsuit Wednesday against two of Jeffrey Epstein's closest confidants, attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico in data privacy ruling
item.description: A jury found that the social media company had deceived consumers for years about its data privacy policies.

item.title: Childcare costs are growing faster than rent in the U.S.
item.description: A growing share of American families are having to shell out more than $2,000 a month for childcare services, new data shows.

item.title: Vance says he's disgusted with GOP "whining" over anti-Acton ad with her estranged mother
item.description: Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday he's "disgusted" with Republicans "whining" over an attack ad from Vivek Ramaswamy in the Ohio governor's race featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother. Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, whose husband was accused of raping Acton when she was a child, calls Acton a liar in the ad.

item.title: Armed federal agents knock on doors looking for noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed and in uniform, agents from the Department of Homeland Security have been knocking on doors to ask residents about their immigration status whether they're registered to vote.

item.title: Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to SpaceX network, sources say
item.description: A decision by Elon Musk led to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's satellite communications network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Armed DHS agents knocking on doors in search for possible noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed federal agents have knocked on doors in some states searching for any potential noncitizen voters ahead of midterms, a CBS News investigation found. CBS News investigative reporter Madeleine May reports.

item.title: Ukraine's SpaceX satellite ordeal sparks concern over tech owners' accountability
item.description: Elon Musk's decision to restrict Ukrainians' access to the SpaceX satellite network has sparked concern over how much power tech owners hold. CBS News contributor and Marine Corps veteran Elliot Ackerman has more.

item.title: Video shows moments leading up to police fatally shooting toddler
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general announced the police officer will not be charged in connection with the killing of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley.

item.title: Ukrainian reporter on how critical SpaceX satellites are to Ukraine's defense against Russia
item.description: Sources tell CBS News that Elon Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to the SpaceX satellite network. Francis Farrell, senior reporter for the Kyiv Independent, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Why can't Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis' deadly attacks?
item.description: Experts tell CBS News geography, interceptor shortages and evolving Houthi tactics are helping the Iranian proxy menace Saudi Arabia, and global energy supplies.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects bid to restrict treatments for trans inmates
item.description: In an unsigned order, the Supreme Court rejected an emergency appeal seeking to revive a policy ending certain medical treatments for transgender inmates.

item.title: 10/20: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Fourteen days until midterm contests; President Trump looks to boost Republicans in North Carolina elections.

item.title: Khanna to campaign in Nebraska with Senate candidate Dan Osborn
item.description: Dan Osborn, who says he won't caucus with Republicans or Democrats if he wins, is campaigning with Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna Saturday.

item.title: Theranos whistleblower calls Holmes "almost unrecognizable" in film
item.description: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz said he "was pretty shocked" by the version of Elizabeth Holmes he saw onscreen in the new documentary "You Can See Everything."

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Sacha Baron Cohen
item.description: Actor Sacha Baron Cohen breaks down his iconic characters: Ali G, Bruno and Borat. He also explains the complexities behind his brand of undercover comedy.

item.title: How life insurance can fit into a retirement planning strategy
item.description: Life insurance may play a bigger role in a retirement strategy than many Americans realize. Here's how.

item.title: LeBron James heading to Philly in deal with 76ers
item.description: The Sixers' wild offseason continued Friday when they added four-time NBA champion LeBron James.

item.title: Lakers land Luka Dončić in blockbuster trade that sends Anthony Davis to Mavericks
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have acquired star guard Luka Doncic in a stunning trade that sees Anthony Davis heading to the Dallas Mavericks, according to reports from ESPN.
